one_line: A shared WebMCP-native marketplace workspace for human-agent discovery and deal preparation.
what_it_does: Lets people and outside agents browse listings, organize boards, research candidates, and draft offers in shared durable state while humans approve consequential actions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes structured marketplace state and focused tools to an external agent, enabling shared boards, cited research, comparison, and approval-gated commerce beyond brittle UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes shared durable canvas, structured listings, boards, research notebooks, offers, and pending human approvals.
Frame sheets visibly show marketplace grids, item detail, contextual agent UI, and a research notebook alongside the listing.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, unusually broad marketplace workflow with consistent visual product surfaces and a detailed end-to-end narration, though the screenshot is packaging and the demo frames are contact sheets.
execution_evidence: 165-second transcript covers signed-out setup, sign-in rediscovery, browsing, comparison, research, offer drafting, and approval boundaries.
Frames show polished landing, listing grid, boat detail, and shared research states.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete pain point for people researching unusual high-consideration purchases and coordinating evidence and negotiations.
impact_evidence: About text identifies lost finds, rigid alerts, scattered research, and difficult multi-party trades.
Workflow visibly keeps the listing and research context together.
creativity_rationale: The outside-agent, human-controlled commerce canvas and persistent shared workbench are a fresh synthesis pursued across discovery, research, and trade workflows.
creativity_evidence: Pitch explicitly rejects embedding its own AI and centers trusted outside agents.
Transcript describes structured shared memory and human-only verification boundaries.
usability_note: Strong visual hierarchy and staged setup; breadth may create complexity.
standouts: Shared marketplace canvas with explicit human approval boundary
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP delta, clear audience pain, and substantial coherent evidence.

one_line: A browser-local visual map of a Notion workspace shared with agents.
what_it_does: Imports a Notion export and renders databases as islands and relations as routes, with WebMCP tools for mapping, reading, highlighting, and annotation.
leverage_rationale: Structured map tools let an agent read and manipulate the same visual workspace precisely, but the core mapping result is also directly available through the UI.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies four tools: draw map, read structured data, highlight sets, annotate islands.
Frames visibly show a generated node/island map with controls and details panel.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a clear, focused import-to-map workflow and polished visual evidence, but no submitted video despite frame-sheet references and limited proof of agent invocation.
execution_evidence: About text explains local ZIP import and browser rendering.
Frames show landing page followed by connected workspace map states.
Devpost screenshot shows coherent project packaging.
impact_rationale: Notion consultants, teams, and nontechnical stakeholders have a real need to understand complex workspace structure visually.
impact_evidence: About text identifies page-by-page schema comprehension as the problem.
Visible map labels include Projects, Clients, Tasks, Meetings, and Knowledge.
creativity_rationale: The island-and-route metaphor is memorable and well matched to workspace topology, though the underlying visualization category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Databases become islands, relations routes, and isolated bases are flagged.
Concept is presented as a teaching and discussion interface.
usability_note: Simple import promise and playful visual language support approachable exploration.
red_flags: No actual submitted video; frame sheets provide indirect workflow evidence.
standouts: Strong visual metaphor for database topology
advance_reason: Focused, useful visualization with credible WebMCP collaboration despite thinner execution evidence.

one_line: A live block-structured LaTeX editor co-authored with an agent.
what_it_does: Renders LaTeX blocks live and lets an agent inspect errors, update precise blocks, insert labeled equations and references, and leave comments.
leverage_rationale: Stable block identities, render errors, equation numbering, references, comments, and surgical updates make agent collaboration materially different from copy-paste chat editing.
leverage_evidence: Transcript demonstrates structured error returned with block ID and suggested fix, followed by targeted update and immediate rerender.
About text lists 15 imperative tools and a declarative form for live document structure.
execution_rationale: The narrated demo shows a complete, coherent core loop from seeded compile error through repair, insertion, reference resolution, and commenting, with matching UI evidence.
execution_evidence: 151-second video transcript explicitly narrates error, fix, product-rule insertion, numbering, label/reference resolution, and margin comment.
Frame sheets show split source/preview editor and changing render states.
impact_rationale: Technical writers, students, researchers, and mathematicians face exactly the stale-snapshot and compile-error friction addressed here.
impact_evidence: About text describes copy-paste debugging workflow and live renderer catching syntax slips.
Demo uses a concrete alpha/alpa error and product-rule equation.
creativity_rationale: The block-identity and live-render-aware coauthoring model is a strong original interaction for technical writing.
creativity_evidence: Agent edits blocks rather than replacing a document string.
Equation labels and references remain live and resolvable.
usability_note: Split source/preview, precise attribution, and undo support make the workflow legible.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage with end-to-end demonstrated execution.

one_line: A parametric 3D pottery editor that deterministically exports buildable templates with agent assistance.
what_it_does: Uses agent-supplied design parameters for complex vessel geometry while the app generates precise, reversible, multipage printable templates.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets an agent control parameters while deterministic application geometry solves precision and repeatability that chat-generated PDFs cannot reliably provide.
leverage_evidence: Transcript contrasts nondeterministic agent output with deterministic app-generated templates.
Frames and gallery evidence show parametric editor and template-oriented workflow.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a focused editor, agent pairing, reversible changes, and a concrete export target, with a substantial narrated demo.
execution_evidence: 179-second transcript shows pairing, parameter update, synchronized browser, and undo/redo.
About text describes multipage printable PDF and design controls.
impact_rationale: Potters have a specific costly failure mode—misaligned physical templates—and this directly targets it.
impact_evidence: About text describes cereal-box template workflow and failures discovered after studio work.
Product output is explicitly a multipage printable template true to the 3D shape.
creativity_rationale: The combination of conversational shape ideation and deterministic fabrication geometry is novel, memorable, and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Agent handles difficult design changes while app owns exact unfolding/export.
Cross-browser pairing and reversible shared edits extend the interaction model.
usability_note: Pairing adds setup complexity, but reversibility and parameter controls help.
standouts: Deterministic bridge from AI ideation to physical fabrication
advance_reason: High-impact niche workflow with distinctive WebMCP-plus-deterministic geometry design.

one_line: A shared job-search workspace where agents find, score, and draft while humans approve actions.
what_it_does: Combines job board, application tracker, profile/docs, agent search and scoring, tailored letters, notes, and approval-gated pipeline changes.
leverage_rationale: Shared live page state and staged actions improve agent reliability over chat or UI driving, but the workflow remains a familiar productivity application.
leverage_evidence: About text describes same-session job board, tracker, profile, and shared activity feed.
Agent state changes are explicitly pending until human approval.
execution_rationale: The written packet describes a coherent product, but there is no video and the supplied frame-sheet evidence is not reliably legible as a completed end-to-end workflow.
execution_evidence: About text lists core surfaces and Next.js implementation.
Devpost packaging indicates multiple product sections, but not observed completion.
impact_rationale: Job seekers have a clear, substantial, repetitive workflow where assistance with discovery and tailored applications is valuable.
impact_evidence: Pitch names search, scoring, drafting, and human approval as the central loop.
About text grounds the problem in job application friction.
creativity_rationale: The shared human-agent job pipeline is useful and well framed, but is a conventional agentic productivity synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Approval feed and same-page collaboration are the main differentiators.
usability_note: Clear four-surface organization and approvals; breadth could increase cognitive load.
red_flags: No submitted video; execution evidence is primarily descriptive.
standouts: Human approval feed for every agent state change
advance_reason: Clear audience and credible workflow, but advance confidence is limited by thin observed evidence.

one_line: A role-aware shared housing-enforcement case page for tenants and legal-aid advocates.
what_it_does: Combines public HPD/311 evidence, role-specific WebMCP tools, condition logging, evidence requests, action packets, and human-controlled filing.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is integral to the multi-window, role-scoped collaboration: each agent sees precise capabilities against shared case state, with server-enforced authorization and declarative forms.
leverage_evidence: Transcript demonstrates tenant and advocate windows with different tool sets and a forged write receiving 403.
Agent actions share evidence across windows without reload while humans confirm filings.
execution_rationale: The 131-second demo presents a concrete case from public data through code matching, evidence confirmation, packet assembly, and filing boundaries with strong coherent detail.
execution_evidence: Transcript gives specific building, 102 open class C violations, 601 days, 68-degree rule, evidence request, packet, and 311 form.
Frames show the case interface and role-specific workflow states.
impact_rationale: It addresses an urgent, specific housing and legal-aid problem where evidence organization and role boundaries can materially help vulnerable tenants.
impact_evidence: Concrete tenant heat conditions and NYC enforcement records are central to the demonstrated case.
Human confirmation is required for condition logging and 311 submission.
creativity_rationale: Role-scoped agents on one shared case with server-derived capability keys and mutual evidence exchange is an unusually deep use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Tenant and advocate receive distinct tools on the same origin and case.
Server re-derives authorization on every write and supports cross-window evidence flow.
usability_note: Role-specific tools and confirmation cards reduce risk, though legal workflows remain complex.
advance_reason: Best-in-packet combination of WebMCP indispensability, observed execution, and urgent real-world impact.

one_line: A storefront where an agent shops alongside a human but cannot complete purchase.
what_it_does: Provides shared catalog search, comparison, policy lookup, cart actions, price watching, autonomy limits, spending caps, and a WebAuthn-gated human checkout.
leverage_rationale: The product uses page-native tools over exact live cart state and makes the confirmation boundary machine-enforced, reducing ambiguity and unsafe autonomous purchase behavior.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies checkout always returns confirmation_required and never mutates the cart.
Autonomy dial and spending cap produce machine-readable refusal codes; confirm-purchase is not a registered tool and is WebAuthn gated.
execution_rationale: The written packet is technically specific and coherent, but no video was submitted and frame-sheet evidence is unavailable for reliable verification.
execution_evidence: About text enumerates bounded tools and explicit checkout safety behavior.
Project facts report live demo and the Devpost packaging is present, but observed completion is thin.
impact_rationale: Online shoppers can benefit from agent assistance while retaining meaningful control over spending and final purchase authorization.
impact_evidence: Pitch centers on browse together but only human can buy.
Specific return-policy, cart, price-watch, cap, and refusal workflows address concrete shopping needs.
creativity_rationale: The explicit anti-finalize-cart design and WebAuthn-only confirmation is a thoughtful, memorable interaction model for agentic commerce.
creativity_evidence: Checkout is exposed for preparation but structurally incapable of purchase.
The spec's safety concern is turned into a concrete product boundary.
usability_note: Bounded autonomy and clear confirmation gate should make agent behavior understandable.
red_flags: No submitted video; implementation claims rely mainly on written description.
advance_reason: Strong safety-centered commerce design and meaningful WebMCP delta, with execution uncertainty from absent video.

one_line: A shared 1024×1024 pixel-art canvas edited by humans and agents in one browser session.
what_it_does: Offers pixel editing, selections, transformations, undo, import/export, and page-native tools for drawing, reading, viewing, and exporting the same canvas.
leverage_rationale: Structured canvas reads and pixel operations over a shared undo timeline let an agent continue and revise human artwork precisely rather than merely generate a replacement image.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies draw/read/selection/edit/view/export tools and shared canvas plus undo stack.
Agent actions appear in a notice feed and use the same verbs as the person.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and technically plausible, with a focused static app description, but no video and no legible observed frame evidence in the packet.
execution_evidence: About text clearly enumerates editor capabilities and no-backend architecture.
Facts report a live demo and public repo, but submitted video is absent.
impact_rationale: Pixel artists and hobbyists have a real desire for iterative human-agent co-creation rather than one-shot generation.
impact_evidence: About text identifies the limitation of generate-and-regenerate tools.
Shared editing, undo, PNG import/export support a credible creative workflow.
creativity_rationale: Two hands on one pixel document, including agent continuation of human edits and shared undo, is a fresh interaction model for generative art.
creativity_evidence: The concept explicitly rejects finished-image generation as the endpoint.
Agent and person share one canvas and timeline.
usability_note: Familiar pixel-editor primitives and shared undo make collaboration approachable.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame sheets are referenced but not successfully inspectable in this review.
standouts: Shared pixel-level canvas and undo history
advance_reason: Distinctive creative collaboration model with credible WebMCP rationale, though evidence is limited.

one_line: A shared ad-account decision memo where agent findings require verified metric citations.
what_it_does: Lets agents file metric-backed findings into a collaborative memo; the app re-reads cited values, accepts or dismisses claims, and supports analyst/skeptic/strategist roles.
leverage_rationale: Page-native tools enforce a structured evidence boundary: claims cannot land unless cited metrics are revalidated, and multiple agent roles share the memo.
leverage_evidence: About text says file_finding re-reads cited metrics and refuses incorrect values.
Shared memo supports human accept/dismiss and three agent roles for analyst, skeptic, and strategist.
execution_rationale: The concept and workflow are detailed and coherent with strong gallery evidence, but no video was submitted and end-to-end runtime is not directly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: About text describes citations, verification, dismissal history, and Monday action planning.
Facts report nine gallery images and a live demo.
impact_rationale: Media buyers and analyst teams have a concrete recurring burden of assembling defensible cross-campaign performance memos.
impact_evidence: About text identifies five campaigns and thirteen ad sets as the manual evidence burden.
Verified citations make claims actionable and auditable.
creativity_rationale: The claim-verification gate and explicit analyst/skeptic/strategist multi-agent memo are a strong original workflow beyond generic summarization.
creativity_evidence: Incorrectly cited findings are rejected before entering the memo.
Dismissed claims remain visible with reasons for longitudinal decision context.
usability_note: Citation links and accept/dismiss states create an understandable review loop.
red_flags: No submitted video; runtime and agent invocation are claimed rather than observed.
standouts: Verified citation gate before findings land
advance_reason: Strong evidence-integrity concept for a real analyst workflow; execution observation is limited.
